liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Mason's Children** (5 reviews): Called the best version the band played, with Jerry taking one of his great solos; Described as blazing hot [5][6][7][9][13]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (1 review, 1 other source): Recommended alongside Mason's Children as a reason to download the show; This version of Love Light has cuts [3][8]

## The recordings

- **gd69-12-28.sbd.cotsman.8999.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 11 songs; 91 min; rated 4.39/5 by 31 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds this digital copy cleaner than the cassette they had listened to for years; Sounds like a monitor mix that runs hot and slightly distorts, especially when everyone sings; Quality is good, though not the best [1][4][8][10][11][15]
- **gd1969-12-28.sbd.cotsman.6030.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 11 songs; 84 min; rated 3.5/5 by 6 [2]. Said about its sound: Cassette master has rough spots, especially in Black Peter, but is very listenable overall [2]
- **gd1969-12-28.sbd.gmb.96578.flac16**: soundboard; 5 songs; 48 min; rated 2/5 by 2 [3]. Said about its sound: The recording has great depth; the uploader suspects it is an audience tape made on stage [3]

## Around the show

- Raw energy and a strong connection between the band and the audience [4]
- The stage banter between songs is a highlight of the show [5]
- Stage banter is funny, and band and crowd seem to feed off each other [6]
- The talking between songs conveys the atmosphere of the night [7]
- The stage banter alone makes the show worth downloading [9]
- Reviewer sees it as a strong Pigpen showcase [15]
- Show may be incomplete, with perhaps one or two songs before Black Peter [2]
- Reviewer claims this is the best show of 1969 for playing and crowd interaction [10]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd69-12-28.sbd.cotsman.8999.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by David Litfin and JCotsman; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Composite of two sources; a master cassette covers Black Peter to the Good Lovin' drum solo, plus the end of Lovelight [1]
- **gd1969-12-28.sbd.cotsman.6030.sbefail.shnf**: taped by David Litfin; transferred by Jeff Cotsman; source: SBD>MC>D>CD>EAC>SHN [2]. Also: Mason's Children was patched in from an unknown-lineage bootleg because the main source had tape warble [2]
- **gd1969-12-28.sbd.gmb.96578.flac16**: transferred by Bill Koucky; source: Soundboard master Reels > Cassette > DAT [3]
